source.title: NEX: Neuron Explore-Exploit Scoring for Label-Free Chain-of-Thought Selection and Model Ranking
source.authors: Kang Chen; Zhuoka Feng; Si-Han Zhao; Kai Xiong; Junjie Nian; Yao-Ning Wang; Chang-Yi Xiao; Yi-Xin Cao

record.tranche_reason: The study uses individual MLP neurons as components of its scoring method and reports transfer results for groups selected by that method. It does not test whether neuron poles have one or two interpretable jobs, or test the specific attribution-graph claim.
record.gate_note: The reported neuron-transfer results concern the accuracy effects of NEX-selected neuron groups, not neuron interpretability or the one-job shares in V1–V2. No results test the stated attribution-graph and reconstruction-error method in V5, or the explanation tests in V6–V7. Other NEX results, including model ranking and human agreement on E/X segmentation, do not measure these claim versions.
record.test_reason: NEX uses MLP neurons as units for a label-free scoring method and reports ranking, selection and transfer performance of its own method. It never explains neurons, audits poles, scores explanations by simulation, or builds attribution graphs, so no result bears on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude NEX, an HMM-based neuron-dynamics score, segments reasoning into exploration/exploitation (~90% human agreement), ranks merged variants label-free (mean r=0.778), aids trace selection and data curation, and that effective-vs-redundant neuron transfer gives causal evidence for its neuron weights.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses sparse MLP-activation dynamics, a sticky HMM, and neuron-group transfer to score reasoning traces and variants; it does not use neuron-pole job explanations or the cited attribution-graph procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that NEX depends on trace row segmentation and that very short responses may not provide enough E/X structure for stable segmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Transplanting Thinking-model FFN neurons with positive NEX weights into the Instruct model raised reasoning accuracy (+7.77 pp at 8B, +1.99 pp at 32B); negative-weight neurons gave −0.13 and −0.69 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP neuron groups selected by E-to-X reuse dynamics carry transferable reasoning capability between Qwen3-VL Thinking and Instruct checkpoints.

record.problems: For the neuron-transfer result, only two model sizes are reported, uncertainty estimates are not stated, and the text does not state baseline accuracy values or a null-transfer control. The paper's stated limitations also include dependence on trace segmentation and sparse MLP activations.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results measure the claim versions; NEX model-ranking, E/X segmentation, data curation, and human annotation results were therefore not included as rows.

untested.parts: Share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one main job, two related jobs, or not understood.
Interpretability shares in other dense or MoE models and at trillion-parameter scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose as shared feature, recursive generalization vs superposition.
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on interpretable-neuron share.
Neuron-based attribution graphs versus trained replacement models and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: Neurons here are unlabelled units weighted by activation reuse; no semantic explanation of any neuron is attempted, so the paper is silent on whether neurons are monosemantic. The 'redundant' transfer effects are tiny and lack a random-neuron control, so even the method's causal claim is weakly supported.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole shares for one main job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood poles.
Interpretability shares across other models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or models up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose as the shared feature, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Effects of architecture, regularization, or tools on interpretability shares, including the InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons, behavioral explanation, and comparison with a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples fail to predict where a neuron fires.
Automated simulation-based scores for neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Replace FFN parameters for NEX-identified effective neurons with those from the corresponding Thinking model.
rows.note: The paper reports the change after transferring the neuron group; it does not provide a baseline accuracy here.
rows.check: Measures accuracy gain from transplanting the study's own method-selected neuron group; this is the method's performance, not neuron interpretability. State 'observed' has no claim referent.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Replace FFN parameters for NEX-identified redundant neurons with those from the corresponding Thinking model.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a slight degradation.
rows.check: Own-method transfer result (−0.13 pp, called slight degradation); no bearing on any version. No baseline accuracy or null-transfer control stated.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Replace FFN parameters for NEX-identified effective neurons with those from the corresponding Thinking model.
rows.note: The paper reports an accuracy improvement after transferring the group; it does not provide a baseline accuracy here.
rows.check: Own-method transfer result (+1.99 pp) on Qwen3-VL-32B; not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Replace FFN parameters for NEX-identified redundant neurons with those from the corresponding Thinking model.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a slight degradation.
rows.check: Own-method transfer result (−0.69 pp); not a measure of any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study uses MLP neurons as a tool and reports its own method's ranking, selection and transfer results.

tranche.reason: NEX uses neurons as units for its own scoring method and reports only its own method's performance; no result tests a version.

source_check.notes: All four transfer values appear in the Section 5.5 text and in Figure 8: +7.77/-0.13 pp on 8B and +1.99/-0.69 pp on 32B. The 8B values are averages. No baseline accuracy is stated. These are results of the study's own method and bear on no claim version. The text never explains neurons, audits poles or scores explanations.
